input.title: inventory-api: Thread deadlock detected in OrderFulfillmentWorker
input.root_cause: Underlying condition triggered by thread deadlock detected in orderfulfillmentworker causing service inventory-api degradation.
input.resolution_summary: Executed runbook RB-105. System recovered in 55 minutes.

stages.remediation:
{
  "remediation_steps": [
    {
      "step_number": 1,
      "title": "Validate Access and Context",
      "description": "Confirm that the operator has the required AWS SSO role and that kubectl is pointed at the correct production cluster.",
      "preconditions": [
        "AWS SSO role **ProdOperations** is assumed.",
        "kubectl context is set to **prod-us-east-1**."
      ],
      "commands": [
        "aws sso login --profile ProdOperations",
        "kubectl config use-context prod-us-east-1",
        "kubectl get nodes --selector node-role.kubernetes.io/master= --no-headers | wc -l   # sanity check we see the primary node"
      ],
      "verification": [
        "AWS CLI returns a successful login message.",
        "kubectl shows the expected cluster name and node list.",
        "No error messages are returned."
      ],
      "notes": "If any of these checks fail, abort and obtain correct credentials or context before proceeding."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 2,
      "title": "Capture Baseline System State",
      "description": "Record current health metrics and configuration snapshots for rollback reference.",
      "preconditions": [
        "Step 1 completed successfully."
      ],
      "commands": [
        "# Capture pod status",
        "kubectl get pods -n inventory -o wide > /tmp/inventory-pods-pre.txt",
        "# Capture DB primary status",
        "aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier inventory-primary --region us-east-1 > /tmp/db-primary-pre.json",
        "# Capture read‑replica status",
        "aws rds describe-db-instances --filters Name=engine,Values=postgresql Name=db-instance-id,Values=inventory-replica --region us-east-1 > /tmp/db-replica-pre.json"
      ],
      "verification": [
        "Files are created and contain JSON/YAML with no error codes."
      ],
      "notes": "Store these files in a secure, immutable location (e.g., S3 versioned bucket) for audit."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 3,
      "title": "Initiate Write‑Freeze on Primary Database",
      "description": "Prevent new writes to the primary DB to avoid data loss during promotion.",
      "preconditions": [
        "Step 2 completed.",
        "No active maintenance windows conflict."
      ],
      "commands": [
        "# Enable read‑only mode on primary",
        "aws rds modify-db-instance \\",
        "  --db-instance-identifier inventory-primary \\",
        "  --apply-immediately \\",
        "  --no-multi-az \\",
        "  --db-instance-class db.t3.medium \\",
        "  --master-user-password <REDACTED> \\",
        "  --option-group-name inventory-readonly-og"
      ],
      "verification": [
        "aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier inventory-primary returns \"DBInstanceStatus\": \"modifying\" then \"available\".",
        "Check that the parameter \"read_only\" is set to true via `aws rds describe-db-parameters`."
      ],
      "notes": "Document the exact timestamp of the freeze for SLA calculations."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 4,
      "title": "Promote Read‑Replica to Primary",
      "description": "Elevate the healthy read‑replica to become the new primary to maintain service continuity.",
      "preconditions": [
        "Write‑freeze confirmed (Step 3).",
        "Read‑replica health checks pass (e.g., replication lag < 1 second)."
      ],
      "commands": [
        "# Promote replica",
        "aws rds promote-read-replica \\",
        "  --db-instance-identifier inventory-replica \\",
        "  --backup-retention-period 7 \\",
        "  --apply-immediately"
      ],
      "verification": [
        "aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier inventory-replica shows \"DBInstanceStatus\": \"available\" and \"ReadReplicaSourceDBInstanceIdentifier\": null.",
        "Endpoint DNS of the new primary resolves and can accept connections."
      ],
      "notes": "Update any application configuration that references the old primary endpoint to point to the new primary endpoint if DNS does not automatically alias."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 5,
      "title": "Drain and Restart OrderFulfillmentWorker Pods",
      "description": "Perform a rolling restart of the worker pods to clear the deadlock state while keeping traffic flowing through the new primary.",
      "preconditions": [
        "New primary is operational (Step 4).",
        "No pending pod evictions."
      ],
      "commands": [
        "# Label the deployment for targeted rollout (if not already labeled)",
        "kubectl label deployment order-fulfillment-worker app=order-fulfillment --overwrite",
        "# Perform a rolling restart",
        "kubectl rollout restart deployment/order-fulfillment-worker -n inventory",
        "# Wait for rollout to complete",
        "kubectl rollout status deployment/order-fulfillment-worker -n inventory --timeout=300s"
      ],
      "verification": [
        "All pods report READY=1/1 and STATUS=Running.",
        "Log inspection shows no occurrence of ERR_APPLICATION_ERROR_925 or ERR_APPLICATION_ERROR_444 after restart.",
        "Metrics for thread pool usage return to normal ranges."
      ],
      "notes": "If a pod fails to become ready, investigate logs before proceeding."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 6,
      "title": "Reboot Primary Database Node (Optional)",
      "description": "If the primary node exhibits lingering OS‑level issues, perform a controlled reboot now that a healthy primary is in place.",
      "preconditions": [
        "Step 5 completed successfully.",
        "Write‑freeze still active (or has been lifted – see Step 7).",
        "No active transactions on the old primary."
      ],
      "commands": [
        "# Reboot the old primary (now a standby)",
        "aws rds reboot-db-instance \\",
        "  --db-instance-identifier inventory-primary \\",
        "  --force-failure-reboot"
      ],
      "verification": [
        "aws rds describe-db-instances shows \"DBInstanceStatus\": \"rebooting\" then \"available\".",
        "No replication errors are reported in CloudWatch logs."
      ],
      "notes": "If the old primary will be decommissioned, skip this step and proceed to Step 7."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 7,
      "title": "Lift Write‑Freeze",
      "description": "Re‑enable writes on the new primary database to restore full application functionality.",
      "preconditions": [
        "All previous steps succeeded.",
        "New primary is stable for at least 5 minutes."
      ],
      "commands": [
        "# Disable read‑only mode",
        "aws rds modify-db-instance \\",
        "  --db-instance-identifier inventory-replica \\",
        "  --apply-immediately \\",
        "  --no-db-parameter-group-name inventory-readonly-og"
      ],
      "verification": [
        "aws rds describe-db-parameters shows \"read_only\" set to false.",
        "Application logs show successful write operations."
      ],
      "notes": "Monitor write latency for 10 minutes after unfreeze."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 8,
      "title": "Post‑Remediation Validation",
      "description": "Confirm that the original symptoms are resolved and that service health is within SLA.",
      "preconditions": [
        "Write‑freeze lifted (Step 7)."
      ],
      "commands": [
        "# Verify service health endpoints",
        "curl -sSf https://inventory.api.prod.example.com/healthz | jq .status",
        "# Run synthetic transaction that triggers OrderFulfillmentWorker",
        "curl -X POST -d '{\"orderId\":\"test-123\"}' https://inventory.api.prod.example.com/orders",
        "# Check CloudWatch for absence of error signatures",
        "aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /aws/ecs/inventory --filter-pattern \"ERR_APPLICATION_ERROR_925|ERR_APPLICATION_ERROR_444\" --start-time $(date -d '-15 minutes' +%s)000"
      ],
      "verification": [
        "Health endpoint returns **\"OK\"**.",
        "Synthetic transaction completes without error.",
        "No matching error signatures appear in logs for the last 15 minutes."
      ],
      "notes": "Document the validation timestamps and attach logs to the incident ticket."
    }
  ],
  "rollback_plan": {
    "overall_strategy": "Revert each change in reverse order, restoring the original primary DB, re‑applying the write‑freeze, and redeploying the original OrderFulfillmentWorker pod version. All rollback actions are idempotent and can be executed if any step fails or if post‑remediation validation indicates regression.",
    "steps": [
      {
        "step_number": 1,
        "description": "Re‑apply write‑freeze on the new primary (inventory-replica).",
        "commands": [
          "aws rds modify-db-instance \\",
          "  --db-instance-identifier inventory-replica \\",
          "  --apply-immediately \\",
          "  --option-group-name inventory-readonly-og"
        ],
        "verification": [
          "Parameter \"read_only\" is true."
        ]
      },
      {
        "step_number": 2,
        "description": "Demote the promoted replica back to read‑replica and re‑promote the original primary.",
        "commands": [
          "# Promote original primary back (if still available)",
          "aws rds promote-read-replica \\",
          "  --db-instance-identifier inventory-primary \\",
          "  --apply-immediately",
          "# Convert the former primary (now replica) back to read‑only",
          "aws rds modify-db-instance \\",
          "  --db-instance-identifier inventory-replica \\",
          "  --apply-immediately \\",
          "  --option-group-name inventory-readonly-og"
        ],
        "verification": [
          "inventory-primary shows as primary and accepts writes.",
          "inventory-replica shows read‑only mode."
        ]
      },
      {
        "step_number": 3,
        "description": "Rollback OrderFulfillmentWorker deployment to the previous image/tag.",
        "commands": [
          "kubectl set image deployment/order-fulfillment-worker order-fulfillment-worker=repo/order-fulfillment-worker:previous-stable -n inventory",
          "kubectl rollout status deployment/order-fulfillment-worker -n inventory --timeout=300s"
        ],
        "verification": [
          "Pods run the previous image version.",
          "Logs do not contain new error signatures."
        ]
      },
      {
        "step_number": 4,
        "description": "Lift the write‑freeze on the original primary (if it was still frozen).",
        "commands": [
          "aws rds modify-db-instance \\",
          "  --db-instance-identifier inventory-primary \\",
          "  --apply-immediately \\",
          "  --no-db-parameter-group-name inventory-readonly-og"
        ],
        "verification": [
          "\"read_only\" parameter is false."
        ]
      },
      {
        "step_number": 5,
        "description": "Validate system state matches baseline captured in Step 2 of remediation.",
        "commands": [
          "# Compare pod list",
          "diff /tmp/inventory-pods-pre.txt <(kubectl get pods -n inventory -o wide)",
          "# Compare DB instance JSON",
          "diff /tmp/db-primary-pre.json <(aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier inventory-primary --region us-east-1)",
          "diff /tmp/db-replica-pre.json <(aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier inventory-replica --region us-east-1)"
        ],
        "verification": [
          "No differences that indicate configuration drift."
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "safety_verification": {
    "prerequisite_checks": [
      "Operator has assumed AWS SSO role **ProdOperations**.",
      "kubectl context is set to **prod-us-east-1** and `kubectl get nodes` returns expected node list.",
      "No active emergency
